subject.summary: Saturn at one metre to a thousand kilometres: the oblate banded globe with its north polar hexagon and vortex, the ring system from the D ring to the G ring with the Maxwell gap, the Cassini Division, the Encke and Keeler gaps and the F ring, and the seven major moons. Ring radii and moon radii are measured; moon orbits are compressed and moon sizes drawn five times true so that both ends of the system fit one survey volume. The tenuous E ring, 180,000-480,000 km out, is beyond this volume and is not drawn.

facts.note: derived from the equatorial and polar radii: (60268-54364)/60268
the hexagon jet sits within a few degrees of 78 N in the Cassini polar mosaic
one scene metre is 1000 km: globe 60.3 m, A ring outer edge 136.8 m
the true ring thickness (10-30 m) is below the drawing's resolution, so bands are drawn 60 km half-thick
moon radii are drawn 5x true so that surfaces read; relative moon sizes are kept
orbital radii compressed so Mimas (185,520 km) and Iapetus (3,560,850 km) both sit in one survey volume; order and relative spacing preserved
the true 325 km Encke gap is under the survey resolution, so the gap is drawn 760 km wide at its measured radius
the true 42 km Keeler gap is drawn 420 km wide for the same reason

rounds.summary: the first complete draft, judged by the independent critic
bands, oblateness, moon features, callouts; the critic's pairwise read contradicted its own part-1 scores
the same fixes plus the Encke and Keeler cuts and the moon plates; lost on the globe's protruding band ends
after the stop rule: limb rebuilt as one ellipse, ring tone order corrected to the photographs, hexagon rescaled to 0.21 R, callouts anchored on their geometry, Iapetus plate added

identity.feature: full ring system and its gaps

next: the ring shadow on the globe and the planet's shadow wedge across the rings: the strongest depth cue in the Cassini photographs, and not drawn
the D and G rings are drawn but sit too faint to read at hero scale; the E ring needs a wider survey volume
the moon orbits were cut for framing, so the compressed distances the scene declares cannot be read in the system view
band Titan's polar hood and give it the methane-lake dark albedo patch
the shepherd moons Pan (Encke Gap) and Daphnis (Keeler Gap) are named in the gaps but not modelled
